source.title: The Indra Representation Hypothesis for Multimodal Alignment
source.authors: Jiang-Hua Lu; Hai-Ling Wang; Kuo Yang; Yi-Tian Zhang; Simon Jenni; Yun Fu

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: It evaluates cross-modal matching between independently pretrained unimodal encoders using relational distance profiles, a different method from direct tests of representation convergence.
record.gate_note: The paper reports cross-modal retrieval results comparing original embeddings with Indra distance-profile representations, and compares audio model sizes. These are task-level matching results, not direct measurements of whether independently trained models' pairwise distances converge as scale or capability increases. Cited results from other work and the single-modality classification/noise results are not recorded as rows. Table 3 and Table 4 also report Top-10, Top-30 and Top-50 results; these are left out to stay within the row limit.
record.test_reason: The paper takes representation convergence as its premise and proposes a method, Indra distance-profile representations. All of its results are retrieval or classification scores for that method against raw embeddings. It does not measure whether independently trained models' representations align more with scale. It does not test whether one model maps onto another, and it does not vary the similarity measure or inputs as a convergence test. The matching metric is CLIPScore/CLAPScore of retrieved items, which scores task performance rather than representational alignment. Every row is the study's own method compared with a baseline.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors propose Indra relational-profile representations and argue they improve noise robustness and training-free cross-modal matching, with a remaining gap to CLIP/CLAP. Their statement that larger audio models match better is not uniform in Table 4. Indra T→A for wav2vec drops from 0.363 (base 0.413), and Indra A→T is a constant 0.578 across all audio models.
record.recipe_differences: The method constructs angular-distance profiles over samples and evaluates retrieval against original embeddings; it is not a direct reproduction of either cited representation-convergence method.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports different results by dataset, encoder pair, retrieval direction and Top-k. Only Top-5 is extracted here; it does not compare alternative distance functions.

fits_no_version.finding: Training-free cross-modal retrieval between independently pretrained unimodal encoders, scored by CLIPScore/CLAPScore. Original embeddings score well below CLIP/CLAP: about 0.48 vs 1.42 Top-5 on NOCAPS (Table 3) and about 0.3–0.47 vs 1.06 on TIMIT (Table 4). Large audio encoders mostly score above base ones with original embeddings, but not hubert A→T (0.431 base vs 0.308 large).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Independently pretrained unimodal encoders support some training-free cross-modal retrieval, which improves somewhat with encoder size, but stays far below jointly trained models.

record.problems: The reported outcomes are downstream retrieval metrics rather than direct measurements of representational distance convergence. The audio size comparison is limited to base/large variants with Roberta fixed, and results are not consistent across families and directions. No uncertainty estimates are reported.
record.rows_left_out: Table 3 and Table 4 Top-10, Top-30 and Top-50 retrieval results are omitted to stay within the row limit; Top-5 results were retained for each listed model-pair and direction. Single-modality classification/noise results in Tables 1–2 do not measure the claim versions recorded here.

untested.parts: No measurement of cross-model representational alignment as a function of scale or capability.
No measurement of vision-language representational alignment rising with model quality.
Seeds and initializations are not studied.
No linear map, stitching or relative-representation transfer loss is measured between models.
Universal features and circuits are not studied.
Similarity measure, k and input distribution are not varied as a test of convergence.
Plateaus and alternative causes of alignment are not studied.

record.verdict_notes: The paper's only original-sample text is its method's results; convergence is assumed from cited work (Huh et al.). The Top-5 values exceed 1, which suggests a CLIPScore-based rather than percentage accuracy. The identical Indra A→T values in Table 4 are suspicious. The single-modality Tables 1–2 are linear-probe noise robustness results and are irrelevant to the versions.

versions.untested_parts: Only audio base/large variants are compared for cross-modal matching, with Roberta fixed. The study does not systematically vary scale and capability across architectures, objectives, data and modalities, or directly measure convergence of pairwise distances.
The vision-language experiments measure retrieval on paired images and captions, but do not establish that alignment rises as both encoders improve in capability or scale.
Different initializations, shared features and subspaces across seeds are not evaluated.
The study evaluates matching with relational distance profiles; it does not test linear-map loss, layer stitching, or alignment without paired data.
Recurring interpretable features, neurons, SAE features or circuits are not evaluated.

The study uses angular distance and varies retrieval Top-k, but does not compare similarity measures, neighbourhood settings as a convergence measure, or in-/out-of-distribution inputs for convergence.
The study does not test whether convergence plateaus or whether shared data or objectives explain it.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: wavlm and hubert, T→A, base-to-large comparison on TIMIT
reader_labels.reason: The Indra Top-5 T→A values are higher for the large variants than the base variants for these two model families (R29, R31, R33, R35).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: wav2vec base-to-large comparison and A→T results on TIMIT
reader_labels.reason: The wav2vec large variant has a lower Indra T→A value than base, while the Indra A→T value is 0.578 for every audio configuration; the scale trend is not consistent across direction and family (R25–R28, R30, R32, R34, R36).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: NOCAPS, all listed vision-language encoder pairs, Top-5
reader_labels.reason: Indra matching values exceed original-embedding values for each listed direction and pair in this block (R1–R12).

reader_labels.label: supports

reader_labels.reason: Indra matching values exceed original-embedding values in the listed conditions (R13–R16, R18–R24).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope

reader_labels.label: supports
